en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes,
Section on the Ocean.
10. The Question on the Limbs of the Ocean “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘five qualities of the ocean should be adopted,’ which are those five qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the great ocean does not dwell together with a dead corpse;”

In the same way, Great King, a yogin, a practitioner of yoga, must not dwell together with passion, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, hypocrisy, spite, envy, stinginess, deceit, fraud, crookedness, misconduct, or the stains of the defilements.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the ocean that should be adopted.

Furthermore, Great King, the great ocean, while holding a vast accumulation of various treasures—pearls, gems, beryl, shells, crystals, coral, and cat’s-eye jewels—keeps them within and does not scatter them outside.

In the same way, Great King, a yogin practicing yoga, having attained the various jewel-like qualities of the paths, fruits, jhānas, liberations, meditative absorptions, attainments, insight, and direct knowledges, should keep them concealed and not bring them out.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the ocean that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the great ocean dwells together with the great beings.
In the same way, great king, a yogin, a practitioner of yoga, [should rely on] one who is of few desires,
contented, an upholder of the ascetic practices, living in effacement, perfect in conduct, modest, virtuous, venerable, worthy of esteem, one who speaks,
who is patient with what is said, who reproves, who censures evil, who advises, instructs, informs, demonstrates, encourages, and inspires.
One should dwell in dependence upon a spiritual friend who is a fellow practitioner of the holy life.
This, Great King, is the third quality of the great ocean that should be adopted.

Furthermore, Great King, even when filled by hundreds of thousands of rivers such as the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—all overflowing with fresh water—and even when filled by torrents of water from the sky, the great ocean does not overstep its own shore.

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a yogāvacara, should not intentionally transgress a training rule for the sake of gain, honor, fame, salutation, respect, or worship, nor even for the sake of his life.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality to be taken from the great ocean.
And this, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the God above Gods:
“Just as, great king, the great ocean is stable in nature and does not overstep its shore,
even so, great king, whatever training rule has been laid down by me for my disciples, my disciples do not overstep it, even for the sake of their lives. Furthermore, great king,
the great ocean is never filled by all the rivers— the Ganges, the Yamunā, the Aciravatī, the Sarabhū, and the Mahī— nor even by torrents of water from the sky.

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the spiritual life, should not be satisfied even while hearing, retaining, and discerning the excellent ninefold teaching of the Victor—
the Abhidhamma, the Vinaya, the profound Suttantas, the analysis of phrases, the application of words, the connection of words,
and the division of words— through recitation, questioning, and study. This, Great King, is the fifth quality of the great ocean that should be adopted.
This was also spoken, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God above Gods, in the Sutasoma Jātaka:
"Just as a fire burning grass and wood is never satiated,
nor is the ocean ever satiated by rivers."
"Even so, O best of kings, the wise are not satiated by hearing well-spoken words.
Thus ends the tenth inquiry, "The Questions on the Ocean’s Crest."
The second chapter is the Samudda-vagga.
Its summary verse (uddāna) is: Lābulatā and Paduma.
The seed, the *sālakalyāṇikā* tree;
the ship and the helmsman;
the well and likewise the pilot.
The laborer and the ocean;
by this it is called a chapter.
